content: 1. Bendamustine is metabolized into minimally active metabolites by the enzyme CYP1A2. Ethinyl estradiol, a weak inhibitor of CYP1A2, may increase plasma concentrations of bendamustine when administered concurrently. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Ferrous fumarate can reduce the levels or efficacy of bictegravir by binding cations in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Bictegravir and iron-containing supplements can be taken together with food, but simultaneous administration under fasting conditions or within 2 hours after iron supplements is not recommended. 3. Bosentan decreases the levels or efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of nonhormonal contraceptives is recommended. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Brigatinib induces CYP3A4 in vitro and decreases the levels or efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives co-administered with brigatinib may lose efficacy, and brigatinib can cause fetal harm. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. 5. Butabarbital decreases the levels or efficacy of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Ethinyl estradiol increases caffeine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 7. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, reducing their efficacy. Concomitant use is not recommended, and non-oral contraceptive methods should be used for females of childbearing potential. 8. Calcium acetate decreases ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Ferrous fumarate increases calcium acetate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 9. Calcium carbonate decreases ferrous fumarate levels by increasing gastric pH and inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Ferrous fumarate increases calcium carbonate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 10. Calcium chloride decreases ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Ferrous fumarate increases calcium chloride levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 11. Calcium citrate decreases ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Ferrous fumarate increases calcium citrate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 12. Calcium gluconate decreases ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Ferrous fumarate increases calcium gluconate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 13. Ethinyl estradiol increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while carbamazepine decreases ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during co-administration, and alternative contraception is recommended. Concomitant use may increase menstrual-related adverse effects. 14. Ferrous fumarate decreases carbidopa levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 15. Cephalosporins (e.g., cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, cefuroxime, cephalexin) may decrease ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Ceritinib increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Chloramphenicol decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Cimetidine decreases ferrous fumarate levels by increasing gastric pH and increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 19. Ferrous fumarate decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Co-administration with multivalent cation-containing products may reduce ciprofloxacin bioavailability by up to 90%. Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these products. Ciprofloxacin may also decrease ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 20. Clarithromycin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, while ethinyl estradiol increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions apply only to oral forms of the hormone. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 21. Clindamycin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Clobazam decreases norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be diminished, and additional nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 23. Ethinyl estradiol increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. This interaction may increase antidepressant serum concentrations and the risk of adverse effects. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 24. Ethinyl estradiol increases clonazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines undergoing oxidation, increasing serum concentrations. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Conivaptan increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Cyclophosphamide increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Ethinyl estradiol increases cyclosporine levels by an unknown mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 28. Dabrafenib decreases norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 29. Danazol increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 30. Danicopan increases ethinyl estradiol levels by increasing plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates. Dose reduction of BCRP substrates may be necessary. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 31. Darunavir decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 32. Ethinyl estradiol increases dasatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 33. Deferasirox decreases ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 34. Ferrous fumarate decreases deferiprone levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration by at least 4 hours is recommended. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 35. Deferoxamine decreases ferrous fumarate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Deferoxamine chelates iron. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 36. Ferrous fumarate decreases delafloxacin levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 37. Demeclocycline decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Ferrous fumarate decreases demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 38. Ethinyl estradiol may increase desipramine levels by an unspecified mechanism, potentially increasing serum concentrations and adverse effects of tricyclic antidepressants. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 39. Dexamethasone decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
